highlights.title: Upcoming: Codeforces Round (Div. 1)
highlights.summary: Codeforces Div. 1 round will run for 3 hours on Saturday 12 Sep, starting at 14:35 UTC.
highlights.detail: The contest features high‑difficulty algorithmic problems aimed at top‑rated competitors. Participants can earn significant rating changes, and the round is streamed live for the community.

highlights.title: The Rust React Compiler is now native in Vite
highlights.summary: The Rust React compiler has been integrated as a native plugin for Vite.
highlights.detail: This integration allows developers to compile React components written in Rust directly within the Vite build pipeline, improving performance and enabling safe, low‑level optimizations alongside standard JavaScript tooling.

highlights.title: Grml 2026.09 released
highlights.summary: Grml 2026.09 “Hättiwaritätti”, a Debian‑based live Linux for admins, was released with Linux kernel 7.1.8, exFAT USB boot support, and GNU Screen 5.0.1.
highlights.detail: The distribution pulls packages from the upcoming Debian 14 “forky” release, targeting system administrators who need a ready‑to‑run environment. The updated kernel adds hardware support, while exFAT boot expands portable media compatibility.

highlights.title: Security updates for Friday
highlights.summary: Friday’s security updates were released for Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle, SUSE, and Ubuntu, covering dozens of packages including Chromium, Firefox‑ESR, kernel, and OpenSSL‑FIPS‑Provider.
highlights.detail: Each distribution patched vulnerabilities in core components such as browsers, system libraries, and cryptographic providers. Administrators are advised to apply the updates promptly to mitigate potential exploits across heterogeneous environments.

highlights.title: drogonframework/drogon
highlights.summary: Drogon is a C++14/17/20 HTTP web framework supporting Linux, macOS, Unix, and Windows, currently trending on GitHub.
highlights.detail: The framework emphasizes asynchronous request handling and high throughput, making it suitable for modern microservice architectures. Its cross‑platform nature and active community contribute to its rising popularity among C++ developers.

items.title: Model: ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO-GGUF
items.summary: The Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO model for image‑text‑to‑text on Hugging Face has received 206,575 downloads and 323 likes.
items.detail: The model is provided in GGUF format and was uploaded by ISTA‑DASLab. It targets multimodal tasks that convert images and accompanying text into textual output. Its popularity reflects growing interest in compact multimodal LLMs.

items.title: Model: XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B
items.summary: Spark‑X2.5‑4B, a 4‑billion‑parameter text generation model on Hugging Face, has been downloaded 3,524 times and received 488 likes.
items.detail: Developed by XHToken, the model is optimized for fast inference and fits within a 4‑B parameter budget. It is listed among trending text‑generation models, indicating demand for mid‑size LLMs that balance capability and resource use.

items.title: Model: openai-community/gpt2
items.summary: OpenAI Community’s GPT‑2 model on Hugging Face has amassed 14,739,982 downloads and 3,662 likes.
items.detail: Despite being superseded by newer models, GPT‑2 remains a common baseline for research and fine‑tuning due to its open licensing. The high download count shows its continued relevance in education and prototyping.

items.title: [$] Deterministic testing for multithreaded Python
items.summary: Larry Hastings introduced the Blanket project to enable deterministic testing of multithreaded Python code, addressing nondeterminism from OS thread scheduling.
items.detail: Blanket provides APIs that record and replay thread execution orders, making flaky concurrency bugs reproducible. The project builds on Python’s recent free‑threaded runtime, offering a practical solution for developers testing parallel code.

items.title: 3D Printed Cubes Provide Passive Cooling
items.summary: 3D‑printed lattice cubes can passively cool devices via evaporative cooling, drawing heat as water evaporates.
items.detail: The cubes increase surface area and wick water, enabling heat removal without fans or power. This approach could benefit low‑power electronics, remote sensors, or sustainable hardware where active cooling is impractical.

items.title: COSMAC Elf Turns 50
items.summary: The COSMAC Elf retro computer celebrated its 50th anniversary, marking half a century since its 1970s debut.
items.detail: Originally a hobbyist kit, the Elf’s minimalist design inspired early personal computing. Enthusiasts continue to build and program it, preserving a piece of computing history for educational and nostalgic projects.

items.title: Fixing an Expensive Seagate LaCie Hard Drive Array
items.summary: A 168 TB Seagate LaCie Thunderbolt 3 RAID array was repaired after costly failures, restoring its high‑capacity video storage.
items.detail: The array, used by the Slow Mo Guys for video archives, suffered from controller issues. The fix involved replacing faulty components and re‑balancing the RAID, extending the system’s service life without replacing the entire unit.

items.title: earthtojake/text-to-cad
items.summary: earthtojake/text-to-cad is a Python library providing agent skills for CAD, CAE, and CAM workflows.
items.detail: It enables AI agents to generate or modify design files, integrates with common CAD tools, and helps automate engineering tasks without needing proprietary software.

items.title: radixark/miles
items.summary: radixark/miles is an enterprise reinforcement‑learning framework for post‑training large language and vision‑language models, built as a fork of the slime project.
items.detail: Designed for production use, it supports distributed training and fine‑tuning of LLMs and VLMs after initial training, providing tools for policy optimization in enterprise settings.

items.title: CalcProgrammer1/OpenRGB
items.summary: OpenRGB is an open‑source cross‑platform utility for controlling RGB lighting without vendor software, available for Windows, Linux, and macOS.
items.detail: The tool works with many motherboard and peripheral manufacturers, offers a unified API, and its releases are mirrored on GitLab for easy access.

items.title: GreptimeTeam/greptimedb
items.summary: GreptimeDB is an open‑source observability database that stores metrics, logs, and traces using a single columnar engine on object storage.
items.detail: Written in Rust, it provides SQL query support, integrates with Prometheus and OpenTelemetry, and aims to simplify unified telemetry handling across cloud environments.

items.title: NVIDIA/SkillSpector
items.summary: SkillSpector is a Python security scanner that analyzes AI agent skills for vulnerabilities such as prompt injection and data exfiltration across Claude Code, Codex, and MCP implementations.
items.detail: It helps developers vet third‑party skill packages before deployment, flags supply‑chain risks, and can be integrated into CI pipelines for continuous security checks.
